Sandbox_SL_MasonryWalls: Stone and Brick Walls: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_MasonryWalls_tooltip: Full-height stone and brick walls, window frames and door frames.
Sandbox_SL_MasonryLowWalls: Short Stone and Brick Walls: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_MasonryLowWalls_tooltip: Waist-high masonry such as the short brick wall. Damage is reduced to a quarter, so even cattle need many rams.
Sandbox_SL_MetalWalls: Metal Walls and Doors: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_MetalWalls_tooltip: Full-height metal walls and frames, metal doors on map buildings, and metal doors built at or above the welding level set below.
Sandbox_SL_MetalDoors_tooltip: Metal doors built below the welding level set below. Damage is cut to a tenth, so even a desperate bull needs around 30 rams on a door welded at level 3.
Sandbox_SL_MetalDoorWeldingLevel: Metal Door Welding Level for Full Strength
Sandbox_SL_MetalDoorWeldingLevel_tooltip: Metal doors built by a welder at or above this level count as metal walls. The builder's level is read from the door's health (300 per level). Set to 11 to make every built metal door use the low-skill rule.
Sandbox_SL_MetalFences: Metal Bar and Pole Fences: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_MetalFences_tooltip: Welded bar and pole fences and their gates.
Sandbox_SL_WireFences_tooltip: Wire mesh and barbed wire fences and wire gates. Wire stretches and posts tilt under a big animal; damage is halved.
Sandbox_SL_WoodenWalls: Wooden Walls and Doors: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_WoodenWalls_tooltip: Plank and log walls, wooden window and door frames, and wooden doors (including doors on map buildings). Damage is halved.
Sandbox_SL_WoodenFences: Wooden Fences and Gates: Breakable By
Sandbox_SL_WoodenFences_tooltip: Plank, log and stick fences and wooden gates.
Sandbox_SL_WoodenFenceHits_tooltip: An undamaged wooden fence or gate survives this many rams from an animal allowed to break it, whatever the animal's size, and breaks on the next one.
Sandbox_SL_Furnishings_tooltip: Crates, shelves, counters and any other built object that is not a wall, fence or door. Broken containers drop their contents on the floor.
Sandbox_SL_MediumWeight_tooltip: Animals at or above this live weight count as medium. Adult sheep and pigs usually qualify.
Sandbox_SL_HeavyWeight_tooltip: Animals at or above this live weight count as heavy. Adult cattle usually qualify.
Sandbox_SL_ForcePercent_tooltip: Scales all structure damage from animals. At 100, a 100 kg animal of average strength rams for 100 damage, growing with the square root of weight (a 700 kg cow does about 265). Vanilla, by comparison, has sheep and pigs hit for about 200 and cattle for about 120 regardless of size or material.
Sandbox_SL_PanicForcePercent_tooltip: Force of a ram when the animal is only stressed. Starving, parched or provoked animals always ram at full force.
Sandbox_SL_GiveUpRams_tooltip: After this many rams that do no damage, the animal wears itself out, calms down if it was panicking, and stumbles back from the wall. An animal on a lead stops after one ram so it can be pulled away. 0 disables giving up (the lead still works).
Sandbox_SL_HiddenRunners_tooltip: Vanilla animals get stressed by anyone running within 10 tiles, even through walls. With this on, running only stresses animals that can actually see you; walls and closed doors block it, while fences and open doorways don't. A full sprint always stresses animals within 10 tiles, through walls or not.
Sandbox_SL_HiddenZombies_tooltip: Vanilla animals sense zombies within 10 tiles through walls, gaining stress and bolting when one is within 6 tiles. With this on, they only react to zombies they can actually see. Noises zombies make, like banging on walls, still frighten them.
Sandbox_SL_FamiliarOwners_tooltip: Running near an animal that trusts you no longer stresses it. A full sprint, loud noises and threats still do.
Sandbox_SL_FamiliarAcceptance_tooltip: Minimum acceptance an animal must have for you before your running stops bothering it.
